summary: Bruno Snell (1896–1986) worked in linguistics and related fields. He studied at the universities of Edinburgh (1914), Göttingen (~1919–1922), and Oxford (~1921–1922), and later held a post at the University of Hamburg (~1925–1959).

Bryan D. Lowe specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Otani University and under scholars including Jacqueline I. Stone and Martin Collcutt, and served as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Vanderbilt University (attested 2017–2019).

Bryan J. Cuevas is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Emory University (1987) and completed his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano, later becoming John F. Priest Professor of Religion at Florida State University.

Bryan W. Van Norden (born 1962) specializes in philosophy and Sinology. He studied at Stanford University (~1985–1991) and held the James Monroe Taylor Chair in Philosophy at Vassar College (~1996–2020).

Bryce Ryan (1911–2002) worked in Indology and sociology. Educated at the University of Washington and Harvard University (PhD 1940), he taught at several institutions, including the University of Ceylon, and served as professor at the University of Miami (1957–1976).

Buddhadeb Gorai is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who completed an M.A. at Jadavpur University (2006–2008). He served as an Assistant Professor at Deshbandhu College for Girls (2014) and founded the Bhāratāyana IKS Journal in 2026.

Buddhike Indrasena is an Indologist and medical professional who studied at the University of Peradeniya, PGIM, and PGIA. He served as a consultant surgeon at several Sri Lankan hospitals and was appointed Medical Statistician Associate at the World Academy of Medical Leadership (2020).

Buddhodev Ghosh works in Indology and philosophy. He held positions at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay as a Project-Teaching Assistant (2022) and at the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research as a Project Associate (2024–2025).

Bulcsu Siklós specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed a PhD at the University of London, studying under Tadeusz Skorupski and Charles R. Bawden, and was later affiliated with SOAS University of London (attested 1996).

Bunga Fukui (1934–2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Waseda University and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Paul Demiéville, later serving as professor at Waseda University (~1978–2005).

Bunkyo Aoki (1886–1956) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University and under Kozui Otani (~1910–1914), and was appointed as a lecturer in Tibetan at the University of Tokyo in 1951.

Bunsaku Kurata (1918–1983) specialized in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history/archaeology. Educated at Aoyama Gakuin and Waseda University, he worked for cultural properties commissions and the Tokyo National Museum, becoming Director of Nara National Museum in 1975.

Bunyiu Nanjio (1849–1927) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Oxford under Friedrich Max Müller. He held multiple leadership and teaching roles at Otani University and also taught at the University of Tokyo.

Bunzaburo Matsumoto (1869–1944) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Tokyo. He taught at Rikkyo University and First Higher School, and later served as professor and president (1908–1915) at Kyoto University.

Burchard Brentjes (1929–2012) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Heinz Mode at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, where he later held an academic post from ~1954 to 1980.

Burkard Wilhelm Leist (1819–1906) was a scholar of law, history, and Indology. He studied at Göttingen, Heidelberg, and Berlin under Friedrich Carl von Savigny, and served as professor of law at Basel, Rostock, and Jena.

Burkhard Quessel is a Tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg, where he was also a member (attested 1997). He later served as a curator at the British Library (attested 2002–2012).

Burmansah Burmansah is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned degrees from Universitas Komputer Indonesia and the State University of Jakarta. In 2020, he held a post as a lecturer at STIAB Jinarakkhita.

Burton Stein (1926–1996) was a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Illinois Chicago and the University of Chicago. He taught at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1965–1983) and SOAS University of London (1983).

Burton Watson (1925–2017) was a Sinologist and Japanologist. He earned his degrees from Columbia University, studying under Wm. Theodore de Bary, and also studied at Kyoto University. He later held professorial posts at Columbia and Stanford University.
